gold: Ipsilateral hemisphere hemorrhagic stroke with peripheral-type facial paralysis

selector.rationale: The patient's symptoms, including incomplete closure of the right eye, flattening of the right nasolabial fold, and right-sided hemiplegia, along with the imaging studies showing hemorrhage in the left thalamus-radiation crown region, are most consistent with a stroke, particularly given the acute onset and the patient's history of hypertension.

rejected.label: Corticobulbar tract lesion
rejected.why: While the corticobulbar tract appeared thinner on the left side, this finding is more of a consequence of the primary lesion rather than the primary diagnosis itself.

rejected.label: Thalamic hemorrhage
rejected.why: Although there is hemorrhage in the thalamus, this is part of the broader presentation of a stroke, specifically an intracerebral hemorrhage, rather than the primary diagnosis.

rejected.label: Intracerebral Hemorrhage
rejected.why: While this is a correct description of part of the patient's condition, 'Stroke' is a more encompassing diagnosis that includes the intracerebral hemorrhage as its cause.
